title: Use audited material ownership when authorizing material corrections
suggestion: For consolidated items, determine material ownership from their audited evidence_keys. Keep candidate-source fallback separately for omissions that have no formal evidence. Do not let obsolete extraction provenance expand the authorized item/evidence/source-check set. Add a rejection case where candidate and audited material attribution differ and a material-only correction attempts to alter the other material's passed item.
rationale: Content03 deliberately makes extraction a fallible hint and the formal evidence directory authoritative. However, entry_materials unions formal evidence materials with candidates[member].materials. If c1 was extracted under m1 but merge has corrected i0 to evidence e0 belonging exclusively to m2, a review issue targeting only m1 still puts i0 in affected_entries and m2 in affected_materials. A snapshot-bound scripted-provider reproduction changed that m2-only item's name during the m1 correction, passed deterministic validation, reached review1/history, and returned the changed proposal. The control with candidate attribution also on m2 rejected the same drift before history. This violates approved AC-S03's protection of other sources' passed targets; a later model passed result does not enforce the required deterministic authorization boundary. The retained material-isolation fixtures keep candidate and audited attribution aligned, so they do not cover this path.
